rationale:
Evidence: the only race (iteration 0, 60 trials across oval, s-bend and slalom) ended off track in every trial. Progress was 0.04 to 0.12, with no completions. max_error was about 0.061 m, just over the 0.06 m off-track limit, and rms_error was about 0.03 m. Steering oscillation and control effort were non-trivial. The robot is swinging across the tape and leaving the track within the first fraction of a metre. The limit cannot be relaxed: body_width 0.18 gives max(0.06, 0.0125 + 0.045) = 0.06, so the controller must keep lateral error under about 0.06 m.

Likely cause: kp = 6 with weights up to 1.5 gives turn near 9 at the edge of the tape, which is 3150 PWM of differential. That is too aggressive for the wheel and body dynamics, so each correction overshoots. kd = 0.05 is too weak to damp the swing, and ki = 0.1 is too weak to cancel the fixed left/right motor mismatch, which shows up as a steady bias.

Changes: (1) kp 6.0 to 3.0, halving the steering gain so a full-scale edge error gives about 1575 PWM of differential, which is firm but not saturating. (2) kd 0.05 to 0.25, for damping of the swing. (3) ki 0.1 to 0.3, so the integral can cancel the motor-mismatch bias (integral is capped at 2, so the contribution stays bounded at about 0.6 turn). (4) Sensor footprint 0.012 to 0.016 m, with five sensors at 0.01 m spacing spanning x = -0.02 to +0.02 at y = 0.04. The larger footprint gives smoother readings and keeps the tape visible across a wider offset range. Weights stay antisymmetric. (5) base_speed 1.8 to 1.6, so the robot has time to correct at this gain while staying near the roughly 1.5 m/s needed to finish in 3 s. Geometry otherwise unchanged. The wheel and body values are kept so the comparison with iteration 0 isolates the controller and sensor changes.

Expected result: max_error should drop well below 0.06 m and rms_error toward 0.015 to 0.025 m, so runs should survive much longer and progress should rise substantially on the oval and s-bend. Completion on the slalom is uncertain and may need a further kd or base_speed adjustment once the next telemetry is available. The measurement request covers all metrics so the review can see where oscillation or line loss occurs.
